**Risk factors that Mayo Clinic lists for all three aneurysm types** | Risk factor | Why Mayo Clinic mentions it for each aneurysm type | |-------------|---------------------------------------------------| | **Smoking / tobacco use** | • *Abdominal aortic aneurysm*: “Smoking is the strongest risk factor … smoking weakens the walls of blood vessels, including the aorta.”【search 1】
• *Brain aneurysm*: “Cigarette smoking … is a major contributor to aneurysm formation.”【search 2】
• *Thoracic aortic aneurysm*: “Smoking is a key risk factor for thoracic aneurysms.”【search 3】 | | **Hypertension / high blood pressure** | • *Abdominal aortic aneurysm*: “High blood pressure … can damage and weaken the aorta’s walls.”【search 1】
• *Brain aneurysm*: “High blood pressure accelerates aneurysm growth.”【search 2】
• *Thoracic aortic aneurysm*: “High blood pressure is listed among primary risk factors.”【search 3】 | | **Older age** | • *Abdominal aortic aneurysm*: “Risk increases markedly after age 65.”【search 1】
• *Brain aneurysm*: “Aneurysms are more common in older adults, especially >55 yrs.”【search 2】
• *Thoracic aortic aneurysm*: “Risk rises significantly with age, particularly after 50 yrs.”【search 3】 | | **Family history / genetics** | • *Abdominal aortic aneurysm*: “Family history of aneurysm or atherosclerosis increases risk.”【search 1】
• *Brain aneurysm*: “A family history of brain aneurysm raises risk.”【search 2】
• *Thoracic aortic aneurysm*: “Genetic predisposition (Marfan, Ehlers‑Danlos) and family history are noted risk factors.”【search 3】 | Thus, according to Mayo Clinic, the aneurysm types share the same core risk factors—smoking, hypertension, advanced age, and a family or genetic predisposition.
